title: Aged Care Legislation Amendment (Financial Transparency) Bill 2020 [No. 2]
short_title: Aged Care Legislation Amendment (Financial Transparency) Bill 2020 [No. 2]

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The Aged Care Legislation Amendment (Financial Transparency) Bill 2020 [No. 2] was moved, requiring residential aged-care providers to publicly disclose income, spending on care, staff, and administration, and to submit annual reports to the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission. The speech highlighted that ASX-listed providers Estia Health, Japara, and Regis Healthcare received $8.4 billion in government subsidies and resident charges over five years while paying over $600 million to shareholders, and that 75% of regional providers operate at a cash loss.

speeches.speaker: Zali Steggall
speeches.brief: The speaker argued for the Aged Care Legislation Amendment (Financial Transparency) Bill 2020, which would require aged-care providers to publicly disclose how they spend $25 billion in combined public and private funding, including $1.1 billion in annual profit, citing support from the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Federation and the Law Council of Australia.
